name: jenkins_get_build
description: Get the status and details of a Jenkins build. Use when asked "did the build pass?", "what's the status of CI for this commit?", or "why did the build fail?". Pass sha to find the build matching a specific commit (scans recent builds), or buildNumber for an explicit build, or omit both to get the latest. Returns result, duration, commit, branch, cause, parameters, pipeline stage breakdown (with stage ids for jenkins_get_log), recent changes, and artifact URLs.

jobPath.description: Jenkins job path. Use slashes for nested folders, e.g. "platform/api/build-master". If omitted, the server tries to resolve from the current git remote via repoJobMap (and prompts for a pick when multiple match).

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when jobPath is omitted and must be resolved from the current git remote. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own; the calling harness supplies the path. Ignored when jobPath is given. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

buildNumber.description: Build number (e.g. 42), or one of "lastBuild", "lastSuccessfulBuild", "lastFailedBuild", "lastCompletedBuild" (default: lastBuild)

sha.description: Find the most recent build whose lastBuiltRevision matches this commit SHA (full or 7+ char prefix). Overrides buildNumber.

scanLimit.description: How many recent builds to scan when sha is provided (default 30, 1-200; anything else is rejected). Increase for repos with many builds per commit. A miss reports how many builds were scanned and whether the job retains older ones.

includeStages.description: Include Pipeline stage breakdown when available (default true)

includeChangeSet.description: Include the commits in this build (default true)

name: jenkins_get_log
description: Fetch the console log for a Jenkins build. Use when diagnosing a failure after jenkins_get_build shows result=FAILURE/UNSTABLE. By default returns the tail (last 200KB) to stay within context — pass full=true for everything, or tailChars to set a different cap. For Pipeline jobs, pass stageId (from jenkins_get_build output) to get just that stage's logs, which is dramatically smaller and more focused than the whole console.

jobPath.description: Jenkins job path (auto-resolved from current repo when omitted).

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when jobPath is omitted and must be resolved from the current git remote. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own; the calling harness supplies the path. Ignored when jobPath is given. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

buildNumber.description: Build number to fetch the log for (numeric).

stageId.description: Optional Pipeline stage id (from jenkins_get_build). Returns just that stage's per-step logs.

tailChars.description: Return only the last N characters (default 200000). Ignored if full=true.

full.description: Return the entire log without truncation. Use sparingly — large jobs can produce megabytes.

name: jenkins_get_tests
description: Fetch the test report for a build. Use when asked "which tests failed?" or "why did this build fail?" — surfaces failed test names, classes, and stack traces directly, which is far more useful than grepping the console log. Returns 404 gracefully when the job does not publish JUnit/xUnit results.

jobPath.description: Jenkins job path (auto-resolved from current repo when omitted).

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when jobPath is omitted and must be resolved from the current git remote. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own; the calling harness supplies the path. Ignored when jobPath is given. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

includeStackTrace.description: Include stack trace excerpts for each failure (default true)

name: jenkins_list_builds
description: List recent builds for a Jenkins job. Use when asked "show me the last few builds", "is master passing?", or to find a build number to drill into. Each row shows result, duration, timestamp, and the built commit.

jobPath.description: Jenkins job path (auto-resolved from current repo when omitted).

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when jobPath is omitted and must be resolved from the current git remote. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own; the calling harness supplies the path. Ignored when jobPath is given. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

name: jenkins_list_jobs
description: List jobs in Jenkins, either at the root or inside a folder. Use to discover the right jobPath when none is mapped, or to browse a multibranch folder. Folder entries are tagged [folder] — pass them back as the folder arg to descend.

folder.description: Folder path to list (e.g. "platform/api"). Omit for top-level jobs.

name: jenkins_get_queue
description: Show items currently waiting in the Jenkins build queue. Use when asked "is anything waiting to build?", "why hasn't the build started?", or to see what would run if executors freed up.

name: jenkins_stop_build
description: Abort a running Jenkins build. Use when asked to "stop", "cancel", or "abort" a build. Sends a stop signal — the build may take a few seconds to terminate. Has no effect on builds that are already complete.

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when jobPath is omitted and must be resolved from the current git remote. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own; the calling harness supplies the path. Ignored when jobPath is given. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

name: jenkins_trigger_build
description: Trigger a new Jenkins build, optionally with parameters. Use when asked to "run", "start", "kick off", or "trigger" a build. Returns a queue item URL — use jenkins_get_queue to monitor it, or jenkins_list_builds once it starts.

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when jobPath is omitted and must be resolved from the current git remote. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own; the calling harness supplies the path. Ignored when jobPath is given. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

parameters.description: Optional key/value build parameters (for parameterized jobs). Must match the parameter names defined on the job.

name: jenkins_build_revision
description: Build an exact commit on every Git-plugin job that uses the repository, via the Git plugin's /git/notifyCommit endpoint with sha1=. Use for freestyle jobs with a wildcard branch spec and no parameters, where jenkins_trigger_build rebuilds the last built revision instead of the commit you want. Defaults to the current repo's origin remote, branch and HEAD. A job only reacts when it has "Poll SCM" enabled (an empty schedule is fine) and a branch spec matching the branch. Returns the jobs Jenkins scheduled; follow up with jenkins_get_build sha=<sha>.

url.description: Git remote URL the jobs are configured with. Default: the current repo's origin remote.

branch.description: Branch name, matched against each job's branch spec. Default: the current branch when sha is omitted; no branch filter when sha is given.

sha.description: Commit to build: a full 40-char SHA, or any revision git can resolve in the working tree (short SHA, HEAD~1, a branch). Default: HEAD.

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when url, branch or sha must be resolved from the working tree. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

name: jenkins_get_job_config
description: Fetch the configuration for a Jenkins job as a structured object. Use when asked to "show the job config", "what does the Jenkinsfile point to?", or before making changes with jenkins_update_job_config. Pipeline jobs include the definition: inline Groovy with its sandbox flag, or the Jenkinsfile path and lightweight flag (absent flags read as Jenkins's default, false); any other definition is shown by class. Includes the SCM section: Git remotes (URL with any embedded credentials redacted, credentials id), branch specs (flagged when parameterized) and the IgnoreNotifyCommit extension. Parameters are listed in job order; password defaults are never shown (defaultHidden says one is set), and parameter kinds the tool cannot edit are listed in otherParameters. otherTriggers names trigger kinds that the triggers field cannot represent (e.g. GitHub push); they are read-only and survive a triggers patch. buildRevision.mode says whether jenkins_build_revision will build an exact commit on this job: pinsCommit, pinsCommitWithoutBranch (parameterized branch spec: pass sha explicitly), or notTriggered, with the reason. For Pipeline jobs Jenkins matches notifications against the SCMs the last build checked out, which normally include the definition SCM shown here.

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when jobPath is omitted and must be resolved from the current git remote. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own; the calling harness supplies the path. Ignored when jobPath is given. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

format.description: Output serialization: "toon" (fewer tokens) or "json". Default: JENKINS_MCP_FORMAT, else toon.

name: jenkins_update_job_config
description: Patch the configuration of a Jenkins job. Call jenkins_get_job_config first to see the current state, then pass only the fields you want to change. Partial updates are supported — omitted fields are left unchanged. Use to change description, pipeline script, Jenkinsfile path, build triggers, parameters, or retention settings.

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root) to run git in when jobPath is omitted and must be resolved from the current git remote. Use in HTTP mode where the server has no checkout of its own; the calling harness supplies the path. Ignored when jobPath is given. `repoRoot` is accepted as an alias.

format.description: Output serialization: "toon" (fewer tokens) or "json". Default: JENKINS_MCP_FORMAT, else toon.

patch.description: Fields to update. All fields are optional — only provided fields are changed. triggers replaces the job's cron and scmPoll triggers, so start from the list jenkins_get_job_config returns; other trigger kinds (listed read-only in otherTriggers) are kept. Only description can be changed on job types other than freestyle and pipeline. Unknown fields, including the read-only type, scm and buildRevision from jenkins_get_job_config, are rejected.

type.description: "inline" for a script stored in Jenkins, "scm" for a Jenkinsfile loaded from the job's SCM. Optional when only changing fields of the current type.

script.description: Groovy pipeline script (inline only). Required when switching to inline.

sandbox.description: Run the inline script in the Groovy sandbox (inline only). Kept as is when omitted; switching to inline without it enables the sandbox.

scriptPath.description: Path to the Jenkinsfile in the repo (scm only). Required when switching to scm; the job must already have an SCM.

lightweight.description: Lightweight checkout of the Jenkinsfile (scm only).

spec.description: Cron expression, e.g. "H/15 * * * *". An scmPoll trigger with an empty spec never polls on a schedule but still lets push notifications (webhooks, notifyCommit, jenkins_build_revision) reach the job.

ignorePostCommitHooks.description: scmPoll only: ignore push notifications ("Ignore post-commit hooks"). Default false.

default.description: Default value. Not allowed for choice parameters, which default to their first choice; "true" or "false" for boolean parameters. Password defaults are never shown; omit default to keep the stored one.

defaultHidden.description: As returned by jenkins_get_job_config for a password parameter with a stored default; keeps that default. Cannot be combined with default.

choices.description: Choices (choice parameters only, at least one).

parameters.description: Replaces the job's string, boolean, text, choice and password parameters, in this order; start from the list jenkins_get_job_config returns. Parameters of other kinds (otherParameters) are kept. A parameter that keeps its name and type keeps its other settings. A password parameter's stored default is kept unless default is given.

artifactNumToKeep.description: Max builds whose artifacts are kept (-1 = unlimited).

buildRetention.description: Build discarder (log rotation) settings, written to the job's BuildDiscarderProperty. Only the fields given change; each is -1 (unlimited) or at least 1.
